--- title: "Assignment 7: YouTube Data Collection and Text Analysis" author: "Insang Lee" format: html: toc: true toc-location: right toc-title: "On this page" toc-depth: 3 code-tools: false theme: cosmo execute: echo: false warning: false message: false --- ## Data Collection I collected YouTube videos and comments related to the **2026 U.S. midterm election** before and after Election Day using the exact search term **“US midterm election.”** Searches were ordered once by **relevance** and once by **view count**. The pre-election window covered **September 1–October 27, 2026**. Each ordering returned 100 rows although YouTube reported approximately 1,000,000 results. Only **8 video IDs overlapped**. The relevance search contained 9 duplicate IDs and 91 distinct videos; the view-count search contained no duplicates and 100 distinct videos. ### Pre-Election Search Summary ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Order | Returned| Reported| Duplicates| Distinct|Top channel | |:----------|--------:|---------:|----------:|--------:|:-----------------------| |Relevance | 100| 1,000,000| 9| 91|Al Jazeera English (44) | |View count | 100| 1,000,000| 0| 100|CNN (35) | ::: ::: I repeated the same procedure for **November 4–November 5, 2026**. Both post-election rankings returned 100 distinct videos with no duplicates, while YouTube again reported approximately 1,000,000 results. The two rankings shared **37 videos**. ### Post-Election Search Summary ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Order | Returned| Reported| Duplicates| Distinct|Top channel | |:----------|--------:|---------:|----------:|--------:|:-----------------------------------------------| |Relevance | 100| 1,000,000| 0| 100|Al Jazeera English / FRANCE 24 English (5 each) | |View count | 100| 1,000,000| 0| 100|ABP NEWS (6) | ::: ::: These differences show that YouTube search results are rankings rather than random samples. I selected **NBC News** as a national network, **CNN** as a cable news channel, and **Al Jazeera English** as an international broadcaster. After retrieving channel details, I used each channel’s uploads list rather than repeated channel-specific searches. Reaching September 1 required approximately **68 units for NBC News, 51 for CNN, and 68 for Al Jazeera English**. The final title-filter pattern was: **midterm | midterms | congress | senate | house race | house seat | house majority | ballot | voter | vote | campaign** The vertical bar **|** indicates **OR** in the regular expression. I reviewed **20 retained and 20 dropped titles**. The first filter retained some foreign-election stories and missed some U.S. campaign stories, so I refined it and excluded obvious foreign-election terms. The channel route also identified relevant videos that the general search missed. I selected **three videos per channel per period** and collected at most **300 comments per video**. ### Comments Reported and Received
Show per-video collection details ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Period |Channel |Video | Reported comments| Received|Status | |:------|:------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------:|--------:|:------| |Pre |Al Jazeera English |Obama joins El-Sayed in Michigan rally cry before key midterms | 2,614| 300|OK | |Pre |Al Jazeera English |Ku Klux Klan leader claims rising support ahead of US midterm elections | 16,173| 300|OK | |Pre |Al Jazeera English |US midterms 2026 latest: Trump warns US will burn if Dems win | 602| 300|OK | |Pre |CNN |Midterm numbers are heading into blowout territory: What to know | 7,012| 300|OK | |Pre |CNN |Republican revolt against Trump grows ahead of the midterms | 3,237| 300|OK | |Pre |CNN |I've studied 1000's of data points. Here's my midterm prediction. | 6,833| 300|OK | |Pre |NBC News |How Senate races are shaping up in battleground states ahead of midterms | 659| 300|OK | |Pre |NBC News |Kornacki: Where Democrats see openings for Senate gains in deep-red states | 623| 300|OK | |Pre |NBC News |‘I felt so guilty’ that ‘I had to officially change parties’: Latino voters shift on Trump | 1,362| 300|OK | |Post |Al Jazeera English |US midterms: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race | 1,666| 300|OK | |Post |Al Jazeera English |Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins election to US Senate from Michigan | 2,480| 300|OK | |Post |Al Jazeera English |Republicans fuming after Democrat Talarico flips Texas Senate blue | 1,101| 300|OK | |Post |CNN |Trump blames Fox News, GOP candidates for midterm losses | 8,027| 300|OK | |Post |CNN |CNN's first reactions to US House & Senate flips | 4,926| 300|OK | |Post |CNN |Dems win the Senate, CNN projects | 5,350| 300|OK | |Post |NBC News |Steve Kornacki analyzes 2026 midterm election results | 389| 300|OK | |Post |NBC News |President Trump speaks to various media outlets reacting to midterm results | 921| 300|OK | |Post |NBC News |BREAKING: Democrats win the Senate, taking full control of Congress, NBC News projects | 950| 300|OK | ::: :::
The nine pre-election videos reported **39,115 comments**, while 2,700 were received. The post-election videos reported **25,810**, while 2,700 were received. The main reason is the 300-comment cap; deleted, moderated, held, or unavailable comments may also contribute. All **18 videos had OK status**; none were disabled, empty, or errors. Before joining, video and comment IDs were deduplicated, and video metadata were joined to comments as a **many-to-one relationship**. No duplicate comment IDs remained. ## Quota Plan and Actual Use The assignment called for a quota plan before API collection. I did not preserve a separate pre-call table during the original collection session, so the following table is a **reconstruction of the documented workflow**, not a contemporaneous record. ### Reconstructed Quota Plan ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |API task | Planned pages|Estimated cost | |:-------------------------------------|-------------:|:--------------| |Pre-election search: relevance | 2|2 search pages | |Pre-election search: view count | 2|2 search pages | |Post-election search: relevance | 2|2 search pages | |Post-election search: view count | 2|2 search pages | |Channel details | 1 minimum|1+ data units | |NBC News uploads to Sept. 1 | 68|68 data units | |CNN uploads to Sept. 1 | 51|51 data units | |Al Jazeera English uploads to Sept. 1 | 68|68 data units | |Video statistics | 1 minimum|1+ data units | |Comments: 18 videos, ≤300 each | 54 minimum|54+ data units | ::: ::: Search and ordinary data requests use separate quota budgets. The reconstructed values are minimum estimates because comment replies and exploratory requests can require additional pages. ### Actual Quota Use ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Quota bucket | Used| Limit| Remaining| |:-------------|----:|------:|---------:| |Data | 433| 10,000| 9,567| |Search | 4| 100| 96| |Video uploads | 0| 100| 100| ::: ::: The local quota tracker recorded **433 data units** and **4 search units** used. I report the reconstructed plan and observed tracker separately because they are not equivalent records of every API request. ## Comment Structure and Engagement The final corpus contained **5,400 comments**, with 900 comments per channel in each period. Overall reply share fell from approximately **13.5% pre-election to 8.7% post-election**. ### Reply Share ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Period |Channel | Reply share (%)| |:------|:------------------|---------------:| |Pre |Al Jazeera English | 1.78| |Pre |CNN | 27.80| |Pre |NBC News | 10.90| |Post |Al Jazeera English | 2.11| |Post |CNN | 11.60| |Post |NBC News | 12.30| ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](assign07_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: Likes were highly concentrated: depending on channel and period, the **top 1% of comments received 27%–65% of all likes**. ### Like Concentration ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Period |Channel | Top 1% like share (%)| |:------|:------------------|---------------------:| |Pre |Al Jazeera English | 33.5| |Pre |CNN | 64.7| |Pre |NBC News | 27.3| |Post |Al Jazeera English | 30.6| |Post |CNN | 57.7| |Post |NBC News | 60.3| ::: ::: The most active **10% of authors produced 16.0%–26.2% of comments**, showing additional concentration in participation. ### Authorship Concentration ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Period |Channel | Top 10% author share (%)| |:------|:------------------|------------------------:| |Pre |Al Jazeera English | 16.6| |Pre |CNN | 26.2| |Pre |NBC News | 19.0| |Post |Al Jazeera English | 16.0| |Post |CNN | 21.6| |Post |NBC News | 21.1| ::: ::: ## KWIC and Phrase Analysis I treated each **comment as one document**. Document variables included channel, video ID, reply status, like count, date, and election period. Punctuation and recognized symbols were removed during tokenization; URLs were explicitly removed for sentiment analysis, mentions were not separately removed, and emoji meaning was not assumed to be fully represented. I reviewed **20 KWIC lines each** for “democrat*,” “republican*,” “trump,” “vote*,” and “ballot*.” ### KWIC Coding ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Keyword | Party naming| Candidate| Process| Grievance| |:-----------|------------:|---------:|-------:|---------:| |democrat* | 2| 4| 6| 8| |republican* | 5| 1| 5| 9| |trump | 0| 2| 10| 8| |vote* | 0| 0| 16| 4| |ballot* | 0| 0| 16| 4| ::: ::: Party terms frequently appeared in grievance contexts, whereas vote* and ballot* mainly referred to electoral processes. ### Multiword Expressions ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Phrase | Count| |:----------------|-----:| |house majority | 0| |senate race | 6| |early voting | 6| |mail in | 1| |election fraud | 3| |vote blue | 56| |democratic party | 20| ::: ::: The five required expressions were compounded along with **vote blue** and **democratic party**, which were identified from KWIC reading. ## Keyness ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Comparison |Selected distinctive terms | |:-------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------| |CNN vs. other channels |harry, cnn, jeffries, trump, speaker, schumer | |NBC News vs. other channels |steve, kornacki, latino, vote, polls, coverage | |Al Jazeera English vs. other channels |congratulations, abdul, michigan, obama, kkk, burn | |Pre-election vs. post-election |vote, polls, vote blue, voting, republican, seats | |Post-election vs. pre-election |congratulations, war, civil, steve, happy, michigan, won, blame | ::: ::: Pre-election comments emphasized voting, polling, and competition; post-election comments emphasized reactions, congratulations, winning, and blame. Channel differences likely reflect both news content and the audiences attracted to specific videos rather than channel ideology alone. ## Sentiment Analysis Sentiment was measured by channel and period using **data_dictionary_LSD2015** and **dfm_lookup()**. ### Dictionary-Based Sentiment ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Period |Channel | Mean sentiment| Positive (%)| Negative (%)| |:------|:------------------|--------------:|------------:|------------:| |Pre |Al Jazeera English | -0.334| 22.1| 35.9| |Pre |CNN | -0.351| 23.7| 36.0| |Pre |NBC News | -0.246| 25.0| 35.7| |Post |Al Jazeera English | 0.448| 41.1| 20.7| |Post |CNN | -0.231| 30.8| 36.8| |Post |NBC News | 0.151| 34.9| 25.3| ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](assign07_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: The **dictionary-based scores suggest** that all three pre-election groups were negative on average. After the election, the dictionary scores became positive for Al Jazeera English and slightly positive for NBC News, while CNN remained negative. I coded **40 randomly sampled comments** as positive, negative, or neither. Dictionary and manual classifications agreed on **22 of 40 comments (55%)**. This relatively modest agreement indicates that the dictionary-based results should be interpreted cautiously rather than as direct measures of commenters’ emotional attitudes. Errors involved emojis, insults, slogans, sarcasm, and context-dependent language. For example, **landslide** may describe an electoral outcome rather than positive emotion, while **rigged** can indicate grievance that a general sentiment dictionary does not interpret reliably. ## Comparison with Assignment 6 ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Dimension |Biden-Xi tweets |Presidential documents |YouTube comments | |:--------------------------|:-------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------| |Producer |Social media users |Government / presidential institutions |Users commenting under selected videos | |Intended audience |Platform users / followers |Public and institutional audiences |Viewers of specific YouTube videos | |Selection |Keyword and date retrieval |Document archive and keyword retrieval |Search ranking, channels, videos, API, moderation | |Can it be collected again? |Limited by historical platform access |Relatively reproducible from archives |Less stable because rankings and comments change | |Claims supported |Selected social-media discourse |Official government communication |Selected YouTube commenting audiences | ::: ::: The three sources support different claims. Presidential documents describe official government communication; the tweets describe selected social-media discourse; and YouTube comments describe self-selected audiences participating beneath selected videos. They should not be generalized to U.S. voters or the public. ## Data-Generating Process and Limitations The corpus was shaped by the search term, ranking algorithm, channel and video choices, title filtering, the 300-comment cap, moderation, collection timing, and users’ decisions to comment or reply. Repeated participation also matters because some authors contributed multiple comments. Although no exact duplicate comment IDs remained, **repeated or near-repeated wording, including slogans or similar partisan expressions, may still amplify particular language in the corpus**. Therefore, keyness and sentiment describe the **comments returned from these selected YouTube videos**, not the electorate as a whole. ## Data and Retention Note **Source.** Data were collected through the YouTube Data API using an API key. **Permission and retention.** No YouTube page or transcript scraping was used. The API key is stored outside the public project files and is not included in the manifests. Non-authorized comment data are retained for no more than 30 days. **Method.** The exact term was **“US midterm election.”** The pre-election window was September 1–October 27, 2026; the post-election window was November 4–November 5, 2026. Searches used relevance and view-count ordering. Three channels were selected, titles were filtered for U.S. midterm content, and three videos per channel per period were collected with a 300-comment cap. **Known gaps.** Ranking, video and channel selection, moderation, deleted or unavailable comments, API availability, and commenter self-selection limit what the collection represents. The collection date was **November 5, 2026**, with a planned deletion date of **December 5, 2026**. ## Collection Files The files below contain **collection logs, manifests, and aggregate results only**. Raw comments, commenter names, commenter channel IDs, the 40-comment validation sample, and the API key are not posted. - [pre_collection_log.csv](files/assignment07/pre_collection_log.csv) - [pre_manifest.json](files/assignment07/pre_manifest.json) - [post_collection_log.csv](files/assignment07/post_collection_log.csv) - [post_manifest.json](files/assignment07/post_manifest.json) - [video_collection_summary.csv](files/assignment07/video_collection_summary.csv) - [quota_usage.csv](files/assignment07/quota_usage.csv) - [reply_share.csv](files/assignment07/reply_share.csv) - [like_concentration.csv](files/assignment07/like_concentration.csv) - [authorship_concentration.csv](files/assignment07/authorship_concentration.csv) - [kwic_tally.csv](files/assignment07/kwic_tally.csv) - [keyness_summary.csv](files/assignment07/keyness_summary.csv) - [sentiment_summary.csv](files/assignment07/sentiment_summary.csv) ## AI Use Disclosure Generative AI (OpenAI ChatGPT) was used to support R coding, debugging, interpretation of output, organization of the analysis, and refinement of report wording. All final analyses, interpretations, and submission content were reviewed against the actual R output and assignment requirements.
